summary: Bujumbura Melchior Ndadaye International Airport (BJM) is Burundi's principal international gateway, located on the northeastern outskirts of Bujumbura, the country's largest city and economic center. The airport is named after Melchior Ndadaye, the first democratically elected president of Burundi, who was tragically assassinated in 1993. Situated near the shores of Lake Tanganyika, it serves as the main hub for both domestic and regional flights across East Africa.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Bujumbura city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 8-10 km northeast of central Bujumbura, making it a relatively short drive of around 20-30 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Who was Melchior Ndadaye?
A: Melchior Ndadaye was the first democratically elected president of Burundi, serving briefly in 1993 before his assassination. The airport was renamed in his honor.

Q: Does the airport offer international flights?
A: Yes, the airport handles regional international flights to destinations across East Africa including Nairobi, Addis Ababa, Kigali, and Dar es Salaam, operated by airlines such as RwandAir, Ethiopian Airlines, and Kenya Airways.

Q: Is the airport near Lake Tanganyika?
A: Yes, the airport is situated relatively close to the shores of Lake Tanganyika, one of the world's deepest and longest freshwater lakes.
transport_tips: Taxis and motorcycle taxis are the most common ways to reach the airport from Bujumbura. Negotiate the fare before departure, as meters are rarely used. Allow extra travel time during the rainy season (March-May and October-December) when road conditions can deteriorate.
local_tip: Carry small denominations of Burundian francs for tips and small purchases, as change can be hard to come by, and always confirm taxi fares in advance before getting into the vehicle.
